title: The hypertrophy series: mentally vs physically taxing exercises
summary: Second hypertrophy-series episode introducing two programming categories: physically taxing exercises (big compounds, especially legs, which drain the cardiovascular system and need longer recovery) and mentally taxing ones (heavy, scary lifts). Both are individual: for NH, high-bar squats and overhead press are the most taxing while deadlifts and bench feel easy. Programs should spread taxing days and account for mental recovery.

claims.claim: Every exercise taxes the body by damaging muscle fibres that rebuild bigger and stronger, the basis of bodybuilding; some exercises also demand a lot of mental stamina.
Which exercises are most taxing varies by individual.

Physically taxing exercises recruit many muscles and burn many calories: compound movements, especially compound leg movements, which tax the cardiovascular system and need longer recovery, calories and macros.
Experts often name the full-ROM deadlift as most taxing, but leverages matter: for him the high-bar back squat is far more taxing; he can pull hard from the floor and feel fine the next day.
Although bench recruits more muscle, overhead press taxes his cardiovascular system more because he must stand, brace his core and tense everything.
He can overhead press every two days but cannot bench that often, because horizontal presses stress his shoulders and vertical presses don't, which he thinks applies to many people.
Don't assign exercises to days randomly: too many taxing days in a row means underperformance, injury risk and no gains; too many easy days in a row wastes time and loses hypertrophy.
For most lifts physical and mental taxation go together: heavy squats and deadlifts with perceived injury risk stress you out, followed by relief after a successful PR.
For him the bench press is like a vacation, never stressful, whereas heavy overhead pressing is high-stakes, so he limits how often he goes heavy on it each week.
He doesn't find deadlifts stressful because he trusts his form, but repeated squat injuries left a fear that makes heavy squats mentally taxing.
Mental recovery is underrated; when programming, ask not only whether a lift will tire you but whether it will stress you out.

exercises.name: High-bar back squat
exercises.why: his most physically and mentally taxing lift; respect it with recovery time

exercises.name: Conventional deadlift
exercises.why: natural for him, low stress and quick recovery

exercises.name: Overhead press
exercises.why: more cardio-taxing and stressful than bench for him, but shoulder-friendly enough for every 2 days

exercises.name: Bench press
exercises.why: low mental stress for him but hard on the shoulders if done too often
